title: Per-pool headroom tokens & predictive drain pacing to eliminate capacity spikes during LTS rollouts
creator: Priya Shah
description:
Problem: LTS rollouts across heterogeneous GPU pools have produced transient capacity spikes and SLA blips when node/pod drains outpace autoscaler convergence. Existing wave-based drains either underutilize spare capacity (slower rollouts) or cause sudden admission throttles and token drops (customer visible latency/errors).

Goal: Implement a per-pool headroom token system plus a predictive drain pacing controller that coordinates with the cluster autoscaler to maintain steady admission capacity during rolling upgrades. The system should allow faster, safe rollouts while keeping 99th-percentile latency and request success SLOs intact.

High-level approach:
- Headroom tokens: each GPU pool exposes a small number of immutable headroom tokens representing reserved admission slots that cannot be consumed during active drains. Tokens float with pool health and are configurable per-tenant/pool.
- Predictive drain pacing controller: uses short-term demand forecasting (5m moving window + autoscaler rate model) to compute an optimal drain rate for a pool, translating into per-node soft-eviction windows and stagger offsets.
- Autoscaler SLA contract: define a small temporary burst contract where the autoscaler is allowed to provision ephemeral buffer nodes for a bounded window (e.g., 3–10 minutes) to absorb uplift caused by drain-induced pod reschedules. The controller negotiates with the autoscaler via an API surface (autoscaler annotations + backpressure tokens).
- Rollout gates: combine metric gates (error budget, admission pressure, cache miss rate) and temporal gates (min-time-between-waves, max-concurrent-drains) to dynamically open/close the rollout.
- Fallbacks: if admission pressure crosses a threshold, pause rollout and trigger a rollback via the standard LTS rollback controller. Fallback will also signal the autoscaler to remove ephemeral nodes once steady-state resumes.
acceptance_criteria: Rolling upgrades of a 1k-GPU pool complete within 60% of current wave-based time while keeping 99th percentile tail latency within +5% of baseline
No customer-facing 5xx spike attributable to upgrade activity in staging/prod-canary runs
Automated preflight sim (synthetic load) completes within target without triggering rollback in 9/10 runs
Headroom tokens are configurable per-pool and honored by admission controllers and the scheduler
Controller negotiates ephemeral autoscaler bursts and releases them within the bounded window
comments: 2026-02-20 - Priya Shah: Created ticket after postmortem from 2026-02-18 LTS rollout. Observed 12% admission drop during pool A drains; need less conservative waves without risking customer traffic.
2026-02-26 - Carlos Rivera: Spike analysis shows autoscaler convergence lag ~4–6 minutes for common tenant footprints. Proposal: negotiate 3–8m ephemeral buffer instead of forcing permanent scale-up.
2026-03-03 - Design review (Emma Zhang): Suggested adding a visual indicator in Console per-pool showing current headroom token usage and predicted drain completion time. Filed follow-up DES ticket.

2026-03-05 - SRE (Marcus Lee): Raised concern about KV-cache priming — mass reschedules will cause cold cache misses that increase latency independent of admission. Added a pre-eviction KV-cache priming step to the controller plan.

2026-03-09 - Carlos Rivera: Implemented PoC controller and headroom token CRD on staging. Early results: rollout time down 40% in synthetic runs; 99p latency +3% under load. Next: autoscaler API handshake and safety gates.

2026-03-11 - QA (Leila Gomez): Running preflight harness against staging with mixed-tenancy traffic (50% P99 sensitive). 8/10 runs passed; 2 runs hit an admission pressure pause — investigating tuning of token ratios.
implementation_notes: PoC used an external forecasting window (Prometheus TSDB queries) and a simple linear autoscaler-rate model. We should later replace the rate model with the autoscaler internal estimator to reduce mismatches. Use admission controller hook to atomically check headroom tokens before admit; scheduler plugin to honor tokens when placing pods. Keep the headroom default conservative for first 3 rollouts per pool (reduce token % after successful canaries).
testing_plan: 1) Synthetic preflight harness in staging (10k QPS mixed-tenancy) 2) Small canary: 10% of pool with token ratio 6% for tenants 3) Observability: compare per-tenant P50/P95/P99, admission_reject_rate, cache_miss_rate, ephemeral_node_count 4) Post-rollout validation window 30m with rollback triggers
qa_checklist: Run preflight harness 10x and document results
Verify headroom token visibility in Console dashboard
Confirm autoscaler handshake logs emitted and ephemeral nodes decommission after contract expires
Execute manual pause/resume via Console and observe controller behavior
notes_for_oncall: If rollout pause occurs due to admission pressure: 1) do not manually scale pools up; instead evaluate recent admission and cache metrics, 2) if emergency, release headroom tokens to zero to pause drains immediately and open rollback, 3) follow runbook link in attachments.
